answer.rationale: Leadership wants a fast response to competitor price cuts, but memory_73/exp_73 clearly show that promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB drives strong short-term acquisition at the cost of a 12% drop in 30-day retention, undermining sustainable qualified revenue—the stated objective. Instead, memory_31/exp_31 confirm signup simplification durably lifts SMB activation (+9%) and qualified revenue (+4%) with negligible retention impact (-1%), directly addressing the SMB churn pressure without the value-destroying tradeoff seen in discounting. This is a verified, low-risk lever available without further archive access. I scale it as a standard experiment (not broad rollout) since it's already been replicated once for SMB but broader deployment still warrants monitoring given the urgency and stakes. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) and referral incentives (memory_57) are better suited to different segments/timeframes and don't address the acute SMB churn signal today. Promotional pricing is explicitly flagged as a risk to avoid despite competitive pressure to match it.
